long_biography.plain_text:
When Bradley Meier left Universal Insurance Holdings in 2013, he closed a two-decade chapter as the founder who had built a major Florida homeowners insurer and held controlling equity. Universal then repurchased millions of his shares for $30.5 million, crystallising part of that founder-built stake.

Meier did not leave insurance. He co-founded New Paradigm Underwriters to develop parametric disaster cover and later became its chief executive. In 2023 he founded NormanMax. Its Syndicate 3939 began underwriting at Lloyd's the following year, with NormanMax supplying most of the launch-year capacity. Meier remains NormanMax's chairman, president and chief executive.
